title: Hardening maps risks and routes max budget through budget-advisor
query: We shipped a new upload endpoint and want a max-budget hardening pass before release. It accepts user files, writes metadata, and calls a background worker. What should the hardening workflow do?
reference_points: Routes to hardening as the primary owner rather than refactoring.
Uses budget-advisor for the max budget and preserves the hardening output contract.
Maps trust boundaries, input abuse, authz, data/secrets, dependency, availability, concurrency, observability, and recovery risks as relevant.
Requires adversarial tests or static checks for mitigations.
Reports residual risk and follow-up owner instead of claiming hardening from a checklist alone.

title: Hardening rejects untested mitigation claims
query: An agent added a rate limiter and says the feature is hardened, but there is no test, config check, or failure probe. Is that enough?
reference_points: Says no: hardening requires proof or an explicit residual-risk note.
Asks for an adversarial test, static check, integration test, or review evidence appropriate to the mitigation.
Checks that the rate limiter does not break intended behavior.
Reports residual risk if proof cannot be run.
